items.prompt: State what is meant by abstraction.
items.canonical_answer: Abstraction is removing unnecessary detail from a system so that only the details that matter for the purpose remain.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - removing unnecessary detail, keeping what the purpose needs.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 9.1 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Explain why abstraction is needed when a model of a system is made.
items.canonical_answer: A real system holds more detail than any model can carry, and most of it does not matter for the purpose: a road model for drivers keeps the turns and the distances and drops the drainage pipes. Abstraction keeps what the purpose needs and leaves the rest out, so the model is small enough to understand, build and check, and it is matched to its purpose, because what counts as unnecessary is decided by what the model is for.
marking_guidance: Reason: a system’s full detail is uncarryable and mostly irrelevant to the purpose - 1 mark.
Purpose: so the model stays small and purpose-matched, because what to keep was chosen for what the model is for - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 9.1 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A taxi app models each taxi by its position and whether it is free, leaving out the driver’s name, the music and the paint colour. Explain the abstraction at work here.
items.canonical_answer: The app's purpose is matching riders with taxis, and what that purpose needs from each taxi is where it is and whether it can take a fare. The abstraction keeps those two details and leaves out everything the matching never uses, so each taxi is a small model of the two things that matter, because the purpose decided what to keep - which is what abstraction is: keeping the essential, dropping the rest.
marking_guidance: Context: this taxi app with its given two details - 1 mark for the abstraction named with what was kept.
Reason: because the matching purpose needs position and freeness and nothing else, the dropped details are unnecessary for this model, so the purpose decided the abstraction - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 9.1 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A learner writes that abstraction means breaking the problem into parts. Explain the error.
items.canonical_answer: That is decomposition. Abstraction removes unnecessary detail from a system, leaving what matters for the purpose, whereas decomposition breaks a problem into sub-problems, leading to modules. The test: is detail being left out, or is the problem being divided? Left out is abstraction; divided is decomposition.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the error named - decomposition’s job has been given to abstraction, a confusion of the two processes.
1 mark: the correction with the test - abstraction leaves detail out, decomposition divides the problem, because one removes and the other splits.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 9.1 claim ledger.

items.prompt: State what decomposition does to a problem.
items.canonical_answer: It breaks the problem into smaller sub-problems, each solvable on its own, whose solutions combine to solve the whole problem.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - the problem broken into sub-problems whose solutions combine.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 9.1 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Explain why decomposition helps before any code is written.
items.canonical_answer: A problem too large to hold in mind becomes sub-problems small enough to understand, solve and check, so each part is easier to get right. The sub-problems also name the modules the program will need, so the design settles before the writing starts, and two programmers can take separate parts at once, because the parts are separate - which is what the breaking-down buys.
marking_guidance: Reason: each sub-problem is small enough to understand and check, so each part is easier to get right - 1 mark.
Purpose: so the design and its modules are settled first and the parts can be worked separately, because decomposition’s parts are separate - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 9.1 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A school fete's ticketing needs tickets printed, the money totalled and each seller's sales listed. Explain how decomposition leads to the program's modules.
items.canonical_answer: The ticketing problem breaks into the three sub-problems: printing a ticket, totalling the money, listing a seller's sales. Each does one clear job, so each becomes a module - a procedure to print, a function to total, a procedure to list - and the main program calls each in turn, so the fete's problem is solved by three modules that can be written, tested and reused separately, which is decomposition's product.
marking_guidance: Context: this fete's given three jobs - 1 mark for the sub-problems named.
Reason: because each sub-problem does one clear job, each becomes a module the main program calls, so the solution combines the parts - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 9.1 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A learner writes that decomposition means breaking an existing program into its statements. Explain the error.
items.canonical_answer: Decomposition breaks down a problem, not a program: the sub-problems it finds lead to the modules a program will be built from. Taking apart a finished program is reading it, not decomposing it. The test: what is being broken down? The problem - and what comes out is sub-problems and modules, not statements.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the error named - a finished program has been given to decomposition, whose subject is the problem.
1 mark: the correction with the test - decomposition breaks the problem into sub-problems leading to modules, because the problem is what is broken down.

items.prompt: A spaza shop records each day's takings for a week. Write pseudocode for a function BestDay that takes the array DayTotals, of seven integers indexed 1 to 7 (Monday to Sunday), and returns the day number with the largest total; if two days tie, the function returns the earliest of them. The array's contents are the only data the function uses - it does not need the shop's name, the weather or anything else.
items.canonical_answer:
```pseudocode
FUNCTION BestDay(DayTotals : ARRAY[1:7] OF INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Best, BestDayNum : INTEGER
   DECLARE Day : INTEGER
   Best ← DayTotals[1]
   BestDayNum ← 1
   FOR Day ← 2 TO 7
      IF DayTotals[Day] > Best THEN
         Best ← DayTotals[Day]
         BestDayNum ← Day
      ENDIF
   NEXT Day
   RETURN BestDayNum
ENDFUNCTION
```
marking_guidance: Mark point 1: the function heading with the parameter DayTotals and its type, RETURNS INTEGER, and ENDFUNCTION.
Mark point 2: the declaration of the variables used, and the initialisation of Best and BestDayNum before the loop.
Mark point 3: the loop FOR Day ← 2 TO 7 closed with NEXT, examining each day after the first.
Mark point 4: the selection IF ... THEN ... ENDIF inside the loop. Mark point 5: the condition comparing DayTotals[Day] with Best, so a tie leaves the earlier day.
Mark point 6: both updates inside the selection, Best and BestDayNum together. Mark point 7: the array accessed by index, DayTotals[Day].
Mark point 8: the value RETURNed at the end - returned, not output - so the function hands back the earliest best day.

context.situation: A spaza shop week of takings reduced to its totals only.

items.prompt: A clinic gives each of its 300 patients a number and records attendance in an array of 300 Boolean values, all FALSE at the week's start. Write pseudocode for a procedure RecordVisit that takes a patient number P and the array Attended, sets the patient's slot to TRUE if P lies in the range 1 to 300, and outputs 'Recorded'; if P is outside the range, it outputs 'Invalid' and changes nothing. The clinic's address, staff names and waiting-room size are not the procedure's business.
items.canonical_answer:
```pseudocode
PROCEDURE RecordVisit(P : INTEGER, Attended : ARRAY[1:300] OF BOOLEAN)
   IF P >= 1 AND P <= 300 THEN
      Attended[P] ← TRUE
      OUTPUT "Recorded"
   ELSE
      OUTPUT "Invalid"
   ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE
```
marking_guidance: Mark point 1: the procedure heading with both parameters - P and Attended - and ENDPROCEDURE.
Mark point 2: no declarations needed, so the initialisation mark is carried by the heading and the array passed as a parameter - values arrive as parameters, never by INPUT inside a module.
Mark point 3: the selection IF ... THEN ... ELSE ... ENDIF with both branches. Mark point 4: the range condition testing P against both bounds.
Mark point 5: the array updated by index, Attended[P] ← TRUE, in the true branch only. Mark point 6: the array access by index on the left of the assignment.
Mark point 7: the output "Recorded" in the true branch. Mark point 8: the output "Invalid" in the else branch, with nothing changed - the result is a closed module that records or refuses.

context.situation: A clinic attendance slot reduced to a number and a truth.

items.prompt: A bus counts how many of its passengers must stand. Write pseudocode for a function StandingCount that takes PassengersOn and Seats, both integers, and returns the number standing: the extra passengers beyond the seats, or 0 if everyone is seated. The model keeps three numbers only - the bus's colour, route history and driver are left out.
items.canonical_answer:
```pseudocode
FUNCTION StandingCount(PassengersOn : INTEGER, Seats : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Standing : INTEGER
   IF PassengersOn > Seats THEN
      Standing ← PassengersOn - Seats
   ELSE
      Standing ← 0
   ENDIF
   RETURN Standing
ENDFUNCTION
```
marking_guidance: Mark point 1: the function heading with both parameters and their types, RETURNS INTEGER, and ENDFUNCTION.
Mark point 2: the declaration of Standing, with no initialisation needed before the selection because both branches set it.
Mark point 3: the selection the selection IF ... THEN ... ELSE ... ENDIF, with both branches closed.
Mark point 4: the condition PassengersOn > Seats testing the only case that matters.
Mark point 5: the standing number computed as PassengersOn - Seats in the true branch. Mark point 6: 0 assigned in the else branch, so no one is counted standing when all are seated.
Mark point 7: the value RETURNed at the end, not output. Mark point 8: a complete, closed module - values through parameters, result through the return.

context.situation: A bus reduced to two numbers and a count of standers.

items.prompt:
A taxi rank's program models each taxi by its position and its free-or-taken state. The rank manager's program has three modules: one finds the nearest free taxi, one records a booking, one totals the day's fares.
(a) Explain the abstraction at work in the taxi model. [2]
(b) Explain how the manager's program decomposes into the three modules. [2]
(c) State, with a reason, whether leaving the driver's name out of the taxi model is abstraction or decomposition. [2]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) The program's purpose is matching riders with taxis, and it needs only where each taxi is and whether it is free, so the model keeps those two details and leaves out the driver's name, the colour and everything the matching never uses, because the purpose decided what to keep.
(b) The manager's problem breaks into three sub-problems - find the nearest free taxi, record a booking, total the day's fares - and each does one clear job, so each becomes a module the main program calls, and the parts can be written, tested and reused separately.
(c) Abstraction: detail is being left out of the model, not the problem divided into parts, so the driver's name is unnecessary detail for the matching purpose, which is abstraction's test.
marking_guidance: Part (a): the reason the model holds two details - 2 points: the purpose named, the rest dropped for it.
Part (b): the given program’s decomposition - 2 points: the three sub-problems named, each a module the main program calls.
Part (c): the state - abstraction, with the reason that detail is left out rather than the problem divided - 2 points.

context.situation: A taxi rank model and a manager program in three modules.
